title: LLM fine-tuning
subtitle: A full-parameter fine-tune of a 0.6B model on registry-generated data, finished in minutes, measured on a frozen set against a baseline that tied it.

lede: Capabilities model: my agents were carrying the whole tool schema on every turn. I wanted a small model that holds the tool catalog in its weights and answers one discovery call. Tools change weekly, so retraining had to take minutes. I chose a full-parameter fine-tune of a 0.6-billion-parameter open-weight base model over adapters, because at 0.6B a full fine-tune is fast enough that the usual case for adapters disappears. Because training takes minutes, I rebuild the model the way I rebuild an index. The stop token had silently been setting the length of the returned tool list.
quote: The strongest classical baseline tied the model, and I report the tie.
evidence: LLM fine-tuning: full-parameter fine-tunes of a 0.6B model on one GPU in 2 to 14 minutes at a 17.6 GiB peak, so the tool-catalog model is rebuilt like an index.
Synthetic training data generation: an authoring panel of 4 model families with a gate that polices its own authors and quarantined 336 templated entries.
ML evaluation methodology: a frozen corpus of 2,909 examples with no overlap with a 469-query evaluation set, where recall at 5 of 0.955 tied a classical baseline at 0.949.
author: Corey James
